analysis.time: The measles exposure was reported on September 8, 2026, with a symptom watch period through September 29, 2026. The publication date of the notice is September 17, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The exposure site was a Walgreens located at 11250 E. Via Linda Scottsdale, 85259, in Maricopa County, Arizona. The affected population includes individuals who were present at the location during the specified time frame.
analysis.event: Maricopa County Department of Public Health (MCDPH) confirmed a travel-associated measles case, resulting in one new public exposure site. This is a confirmed event reported by MCDPH.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: There have been 28 measles cases reported in Maricopa County this year, and over 3,000 cases in the U.S. The measles virus can lead to serious complications, including brain swelling, and can cause long-term health risks.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: MCDPH is providing public notifications through media and its online list of exposure sites. analysis.brief_en: Maricopa County Department of Public Health (MCDPH) has confirmed a measles exposure linked to a travel-associated case in a local resident. The exposure occurred at a Walgreens location in Scottsdale on September 8, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. to 10:25 a.m., and individuals present during this time are advised to monitor for symptoms through September 29, 2026. This year, 28 measles cases have been reported in Maricopa County, with over 3,000 cases nationwide. MCDPH is issuing public notifications through media and its online list of exposure sites. Those not vaccinated or immune are encouraged to consult healthcare providers about the MMR vaccine. Symptoms of measles include high fever, red eyes, cough, runny nose, and a rash that typically appears seven to 12 days after exposure. The measles virus can survive in the air for up to two hours and may lead to severe complications, such as brain swelling, years after infection. MCDPH emphasizes the importance of vaccination to protect individuals, especially young infants and those with compromised immune systems, who are more vulnerable to the virus. The notice serves as a reminder to residents and visitors to take preventive measures against measles and other seasonal illnesses.
